messages:
maya: seeing elevated admission_rejects on reserved-pool-usw2 starting ~11:03 UTC, SLO latency for dedicated customers creeping up. 503s for some tenants. Investigating now.
ops-bot: ALERT: reserved-pool-usw2.admit_failures > 5% for 10m (runbook: reserved-pool-throttle) :rotating_light:
maya: logs show a burst of long-seq requests + kv-cache misses, plus a spike of 2 large model jobs from tenant `scale-ai` — admit_failed: capacity_limit in the serve logs.
nora: checked metrics: pool utilization 98%, queue_depth up 7x, fairshare evictions started at 11:07. Tenant weighting pushed heavy for a few reserved tenants.
devon: paging admission controller now. Can we trigger burst capacity? what's current burst window?
oncall-tim: burst window for reserved pools is set to 15% of idle capacity, currently 0 because pool already saturated. We can temporarily spin up an extra node group in the region but it will take ~7-9 mins to be ready and will incur a cost bump.
liam: suggestion: 1) enable immediate tenant-level rate limit for noisy tenants (Scale-AI) 2) route lower-priority dedicated traffic to fallback_v1-small model 3) apply admission smoothing (token-based) so we don't melt the queue.
maya: agree on rate-limiting noisy tenant. devon can you apply a conservative 30% rps cap for tenant `scale-ai` and add a sticky header fallback?
devon: applying now: infractl tenant-rate-limit set --tenant=scale-ai --region=usw2 --rps=0.3 --mode=soft  <-- running
ops-bot: infractl job 0x7f9ad accepted, change will propagate to envoy within ~30s.
nora: also gating large-sequence jobs: adding a request-size admission rule to deny sequences > 4096 to reserved pool and redirect to dedicated-burst queue.
maya: pasted snippet from serve logs: ```
[11:04:12] admit_request tenant=scale-ai model=redwood-7b seq_len=8192 admit_result=REJECT reason=CAPACITY_LIMIT
[11:04:12] admit_request tenant=acme model=redwood-13b seq_len=512 admit_result=ACCEPT
[11:05:03] queue_depth=42 pool=reserved-usw2 avg_wait_ms=410
```
liam: quick check: any network flapping or host-level OOMs?
oncall-tim: no network errors. Some pods showed GPU memory high but not OOM. This is mostly admission control / saturation, not infra failure.
maya: we should also start a region-shift plan for a subset of traffic to use us-east1 as a fallback for latency-tolerant routes — can Product confirm acceptable?
liam: product ok for non-SLA tenants; need explicit opt-in for enterprise customers.
nora: immediate mitigations in place: rate-limit applied, request-size gate, fallback model routing. observability: added a per-tenant alert for admit_failure_rate > 2% for next 24h.
devon: extra nodes requested: infractl pool-scale --pool=reserved-usw2 --delta=+6 --reason="incident 1976543210 temporary burst" -> started provisioning. ETA ~8m.
ops-bot: CMDB update: instance-group ig-reserved-usw2 scaling event initiated by devon at 11:13 UTC.
maya: monitoring shows queue_depth coming down to 18 and avg_wait 220ms. keep watching.
liam: plan for follow-up: 1) postmortem to assess tenant weighting and burst policy, 2) run a capacity forecast for next 30 days for us-west2, 3) consider soft-quotas per-tenant to avoid single-tenant hogging.
oncall-tim: assigning postmortem owner: nora. ETA draft in 48h.
ops-bot: ALERT cleared: reserved-pool-usw2.admit_failures <= 1% for 5m. :white_check_mark:
maya: thanks team. please add cost estimate for the +6 nodes so finance can track. I'll also drop a note to scale-ai PM to ask about large sequence jobs.
liam: cost: rough calc +6 A100 ~ $Xk/day (placeholder) — will produce exact later.
nora: capturing action items in the incident doc and will start the postmortem template.
maya: closing thread once postmortem link added. :+1:
